answer: Stop key grinding in committee lotteries: freeze a public atlas of stake commitments before an unpredictable future beacon is released, then draw tickets proportional to committed stake, not account count. Each deposit can back only one ticket set. A gale of freshly generated aliases cannot search the later tide of randomness for winning keys: late keys wait until the next draw, and splitting a fixed deposit leaves its total winning probability unchanged. More chances require more capital locked before the seed exists.
